bodyPart.en: Back or hip (as given in later tables; the Ashtadasha Stotram itself names no body part)

history.en: The shrine of Puruhutika Devi stands within the Kukkuteswara temple at Pithapuram in the Kakinada district of Andhra Pradesh. The presiding deity of the temple is Shiva as Kukkuteswara, in the form of a rooster, with his consort Rajarajeswari. Pithapuram is mentioned in the Skanda Purana and in Srinatha's Bheemeswara Puranamu.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's back fell here. Adi Shankara's Ashtadasha Shakti Peetha Stotram praises the goddess here as 'Peethikayam Puruhutika'.

en: Puruhutika's shrine is on the premises of the Kukkuteswara temple.
Kukkuteswara is Shiva in the form of a rooster.
The temple's annual festival for Kukkuteswara is held on Maghabahula Ekadasi.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.
